Rationale for Proposed Changes perThe23Theatre BA is currently suspended and only open to those students who are pursuing a degree in Elementary Education.
We propose reinstating the BA for all eligible students in order to serve the shifting demographic of our student body as well as refine our BFA program to introduce more rigorous standards appropriate to a pre-24professional training program.
The Rhode Island Promise Act has increased the number of transfer students considerably, making it highly difficult for those students to complete a BFA in 4 years.
Additionally, the number of double majors/minors has increased making it equally difficult for those students to complete the very narrow BFA curriculum without impact to their other majors (particularly those, such as Nursing, who also have to meet clinical requirements that tend to conflict with our required courses).
A BA offers more flexibility for order of courses, thus making it more feasible for our transfer students and those completing more than one major.
URI Theatre completed an External Review in Spring of 2024.

Among their recommendations was to standardize evaluation tools across our curriculum and instate more rigorous standards for degree completion, including capstone performances and projects.
Many BFA programs also involve standards that, if not met, result in dismissal from the program.
It has never been the policy of URI theatre to dismiss students from our program except in very rare cases of academic failure.
Introducing this type of standardization is possible if we have the option to invite students to our BA program in the event that the BFA curriculum is not a good fit.
Bifurcating our program in this way allows URI Theatre to serve the widest number of students while also introducing more clear standards for our BFA students.
The reinstatement of the BA does not require any new courses or staffing.
Students in the BA program will be taking courses already offered in our existing curriculum but have more choice in terms of when and what they take.

Because our program has undergone some changes to course codes since the suspension of the BA, we include here the courses we propose for completion of the BA in Theatre: Core Courses (total of 33 credits): THE111 (Introduction to Acting), THE161 (Introduction to Stagecraft), THE181 (Script Analysis), THE221 (Introduction to Stage Management), THE250 (Costume Laboratory), THE251 (Introduction to Design), THE307 or THE338G (Creative Dramatics or Ethics in Theatre), THE321 (Orientation to Directing), THE381 (Theatre History to 1642), THE382 (Theatre History: Neoclassical through 19th century), and either THE351, 352, 383, 384 OR 481 (these are advanced design or special topics courses) for a total of 33 required credits.
Optional electives within the major include THE112, THE200, THE300, THE400.
For many students, this would include participating in our production season for which they receive course credit (THE200/300/400).
Students must complete a minimum of 30 credits at the 300-20level or above (these may include 300-level courses offered inside the major or courses offered outside the program).

The civil engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission (EAC) of ABET, Inc.(www.abet.org) under the commission’s General Criteria and Program Criteria for Civil and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.
The department also offers a minor in environmental engineering and the Master of Science (M.S.) and Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degrees in civil and environmental engineering.
Department Mission Statement.

Consistent with the missions of the University of Rhode Island and the College of Engineering (COE), the department of civil and environmental engineering seeks to prepare students to practice professionally in the national and international marketplace in the field of civil and environmental engineering through the provision of high quality undergraduate and graduate educational programs and research opportunities; provide an environment that encourages and supports faculty career development and professional/community service; actively promotes diversity; and maintain a nationally recognized research program.
Program Mission Statement.
Consistent with the mission of the department of civil and environmental engineering, the B.S. in civil engineering (BSCE) program will prepare graduates for successful careers, advanced studies at the graduate level, and lifelong learning based upon a solid foundation of technical ability, high standards of professional ethics, and strong communication skills.
Program Educational Objectives.

Three to five years after graduation from the B.S. in civil engineering, graduates will : 1) Practice and actively contribute to the civil engineering profession in one or more of the technical areas of environmental, geotechnical, structural, transportation, and water resources engineering. 2) Practice civil engineering with an awareness of and commitment to ethics and social responsibility, sustainability, and diversity both as individuals and in team environments. 3) Pursue life-long learning through graduate education, professional licensure, or advanced training in civil engineering or related fields.

Program Description.
Civil engineers are responsible for researching, developing, planning, designing, constructing, and managing many of the complex systems and facilities essential to modern civilization.
These include environmental engineering systems; water supply and pollution control systems; all types of transportation systems, from pipelines to city streets; structural systems from residential buildings to city skyscrapers, power plants, and offshore platforms; and all types of geotechnical systems from foundations to dams.
Civil engineers play important roles in planning and administration with government agencies at all levels, especially those dealing with public works, transportation, environmental control, water supply, and renewable energy.
The curriculum provides students with an excellent background to pursue graduate study or to enter directly into professional practice in industry or government after graduation.

The first year is devoted largely to courses in mathematics, chemistry, physics, and engineering science common to all engineering curriculums.
During the sophomore year, students take three courses in civil engineering including mechanics of materials and two laboratories.
In their last two years, students develop a proficiency in environmental engineering, geotechnical engineering, structural engineering, and transportation engineering.
They can also meet their own professional goals through the selection of professional electives in these areas as well as construction management.
Professional electives are selected in consultation with the student’s advisor.
The civil engineering major requires 120-126 credits.
